steps.text: Combine the cream, sugar, sour cream and vanilla in a medium bowl. Use an electric mixer to whip to stiff (but not grainy) peaks. Chill until using. Use within one day.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Whipped Cream
raw_recipe.description: Better than the whipped cream that comes in the squirty canisters! Spread on crepes, fruits, pies or your favorite desserts.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Whipped Cream

recipeInstructions.text: Combine the cream, sugar, sour cream and vanilla in a medium bowl. Use an electric mixer to whip to stiff (but not grainy) peaks. Chill until using. Use within one day.

review.reviewBody: Great stuff! Based on other reviews, I reduced the sour cream to 1/4 cup and increased the heavy cream to 3/4 cup and it is wonderful! Great texture! This one goes in the recipe box.

I used this recipe for my 2nd attempt at home made whipped cream (I didn't LOVE the results the first time I made a different recipe). This is spot on. The sour cream makes all the difference in the world. This has a delightful flavor and consistency. I did reduce the sour cream by 1/2, as I was afraid of too much *tang* and I"m glad I did. It was perfect. I chilled my bowl and beaters about 30 minutes before whipping. THANKS for a great recipe!

This was pretty good. I doubled the amount of heavy cream for less of a sour cream taste and adding 1/2 packet of unflavored gelatin completely dissolved in 2 oz of warm milk. When the cream was beaten to about 10 seconds away from the stiffness I like I added the dissolved gelatin and continued beating to incorporate it evenly. Adding the gelatin stabilizes the whipped cream allowing it to be kept in the refrigerator for several days without going runny.

I am about to try this on a lemon cake with (frozen) raspberries. I'm POSSITIVE it'll work beautifully with a tiny tweak...Judging by the previous comments, I am going to add a smidgeon of guar gum to the sour cream in hopes it will whip up to a lighter, airier whipped cream....🫰Will report back shortly 😀 Oh my goodness! This was a huge hit! Yum yum yummy yum! I put 450 ml of sour cream in the mixer, added about 3 tbsp icing sugar, 1 tsp guar gum and 1½ tsp Vanilla extract and bear it until it was nicely mixed; next, I turned up the mixer to warp speed and when it was considerably lighted and I could see some good bubble action, I began pouring in 2 cups of 33% whipping cream. After a good few minutes of beating the volume had really increased and it held a fairly firmish creamy peak. Very tasty at this point but i decided to grate the rind of a whole lemon in as well. I really thought it was delicious but that it could still be lighter. Sooooo, I softened a teaspoon of powdered plain, powdered gelatin in a little water, turned the mixer back up high and poured it in, boy! This worked very well, indeed! I split the cake into 2 layers filled it generously plopped around some mango chunks, out the top on and covered the entire thing with this lovely lemon cream filling. I chopped mire mango and scattered it on the top. Once chilled it was a sturdily set stack of deliciousness. 😋 I want everyone to try this stuff so I'm making another for church tomorrow.

This is a lovely recipe. To ensure great results and wonderfully flavored whipped cream I always purchase "pasteurized" rather than "ultra pasteurized cream". Look for it at Trader Joe's and/or Whole Foods. It makes all the difference in the world! Another trick for making a very stable whipped cream is to add some dry, powdered milk while whipping the cream. Use the dry milk in lieu of the sour cream for a more pure whipped cream flavor. Made this way the cream will hold not only overnight, but several days in the fridge.

This is a nice stable recipe for piping. I loved the flavor and texture. I did use 3/4 cup of whipping cream, 1/3 cup of powdered sugar, and 1/4 cup of sour cream. The sour cream gives it good stability and a lovey taste. I chilled the bowl and whipping attachment in the freezer prior to making. I put the whipping cream, sour cream, and vanilla in the bowl first and started whipping adding the powdered sugar slowly during the process. I used a Kitchenaid stand mixer and it whipped up very quickly.

This turned out beautifully! I used 1 cup heavy whipping cream, a half cup sour cream 1/4 cup powdered sugar and a half tsp vanilla. I put my metal mixing bowl and whisk in the freezer for about a half hour. It filled up a 8 oz empty Cool whip bowl perfectly. Thanks

This has to be the easiest thing I have ever made. Very light and lots of flavor. I used the advice of the the other reviews and used 1/4 c. sour cream and 1/3 c. confectioners sugar. I put my metal bowl and paddles in the freezer (while I got my ingredients together). I had no problem whipping it into peaks. Hold your mixer straight up and move your bowl in circles instead of moving the mixer. It creates a smooth and even mixing motion that allows for smooth and even texture. Just my personal experience. No more Cool Whip for me!

I made this recipe exactly as written and it was a little too sour for my taste. It would be great for berries or other fruit that would balance it out, but we wanted it for pumpkin pie on Thanksgiving. So I made another batch with just a tablespoon of sour cream and a little more confectioners sugar and it was fabulous! I could not believe how good it was. Far and away the best whipped cream I have ever tasted. Everyone absolutely loved it and couldn't believe it was made from scratch. Much, much better than cool whip. And for those who have never made whipped cream before be sure and use a taller bowl or measuring cup to mix it in. From personal experience, if the mixing bowl is too shallow the cream will not thicken, ever... and you'll realize it when it turns to curds and whey! I use a two or four cup pyrex measuring cup depending on how much cream I am making. Thanks for the great recipe!

Did like others and cut the sour cream to 1/4 cup, heavy cream to 3/4 cup, mostly because I had exactly 1/4 cup left that I had to use. This was my first attempt and I think it came out pretty darn good. It was the consistency of Cool Whip - not sure if this is the intended result or I didn't whip enough but it exactly what I was looking for. It was a very easy recipe to follow. Saved to my favorites!

1/4 cup of sour cream, 3/4cup heavy cream. Followed the rest exactly. Also added a little cinnamon since this was going on banana cream pie. I liked this better than the 1-2-1 standard whipped cream recipes. Thicker, a little cheesecake-reminescent.

My whipped cream came out perfect and delicious!! I made a double batch, used 1 3/4 cup heavy cream, 1/8 c sour cream (it was all I had) 1/2 cup confectioners sugar and 1 tsp vanilla. PERFECT consistency, light, not too sweet, I loved it. First time making whipped cream for me too. Then I used my home made whipped cream in a homemade cream cheese frosting recipe and put it on home made carrot cake. YUM!!!! KEEPER!!!!
This recipe is so good and also so easy.
Also used 3/4 cup cream and 1:4 cup sour cream- perfect texture and delicious. I am not always successful in making whip cream but this my second time making it this way and it was easy and so tasty!

4.9.22 Easy Whipped Cream isn’t the delicate, light consistency that you normally get (perhaps more like a light sauce?), but it tastes pretty good. One thing that I didn’t like was the sour cream flavor dominated a bit too much (maybe more vanilla?). Recipe doesn’t say how long to beat/mix, but I probably gave it 4 minutes or so at a high speed. Doubtful I’d make again, but at least I was able to use up the last of a container of whipping cream and just about finished off the sour cream that was in the fridge. We did enjoy it over an apple bundt cake for dessert.
Tang from sour cream, flavor from vanilla, it's delicious. Whipped up easily, turned out perfectly. Exactly what I was looking for in a whipped topping! Thank you for this easy no fail recipe!
this is great as a fruit dip for brunch!
Great and easy. Next time I will take the advice of others and reduce the sour cream and add more sugar.
Really unique! But not nearly sweet enough. It was almost a savory cream. I followed the recipe and then after tasting, I added another 1/4 cup of powdered sugar and it was great!
Super easy and delicious.
